name: cloud-contacts
description: Diego's Cloud Contacts — standalone Android multi-channel people hub. NOT a dialer-first address book: each person is a set of reachable CHANNELS (WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, Cloud Mail, Cloud Dialer, Matrix, Cloud Chat, LinkedIn, Instagram) and the person screen is a channel switchboard — tapping a channel opens that conversation in its app; there is no default call action. Sources merged into one identity: device contacts (local phone + synced accounts such as Gmail) read from ContactsContract, plus LinkedIn Connections.csv and Instagram followers/following JSON imports parsed natively. WebView UI over HTML/Tailwind (cloud-news pattern). Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: A0_keys/providers/android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A0_keys/providers/android/signing.secrets.yaml.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list.

libs:core._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ea_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ea_cloud-superapp/libs/, same as libs:core. Not listed in app.depends_on and not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which is what gives every app the constellation-wide debug API (127.0.0.1:38090+, own-process logcat) without per-app wiring that would drift.

libs:updater._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ea_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

channels._doc: THE data-driven multi-channel registry — the app's whole identity. Baked into app BuildConfig as CHANNELS_B64 (app/build.gradle) and rendered by libs:contacts Channels + the switchboard UI. Adding a channel is a JSON edit, never Kotlin. kind decides which person datum makes the channel available and feeds its URI placeholders: 'phone' (any phone; {phone}=raw, {phone_digits}=digits-only E.164-ish), 'email' ({email}), 'url:<domain>' (a website containing <domain>; {url}), 'handle:<key>' (person.handles[<key>]; {handle}). package is a soft hint — the bridge tries it first, then falls back to the system chooser, so absent constellation apps degrade gracefully. order drives switchboard sorting; no channel is a default action by design.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.
